h1: The 6 Best Dehumidifiers Under $100 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six compact dehumidifiers under $100, compared on tank size, quiet operation, safety shutoff and coverage.
summary: The 1657 ml (58 oz) dehumidifier is the best under $100, with the largest tank, a stated 230 square foot rating and defrost protection. NeedDuck is the quiet compact option, OWAAE adds a sleep mode, and NineSky is a plain auto shutoff unit. BEDRED and ToLife are lighting-led picks with thin specs.
intro: Compact dehumidifiers are a different animal from the heavy compressor units sold for flooded basements, and the common mistake is expecting one to behave like the other. They exist to take the edge off a bedroom, a closet or a bathroom. Whether you live happily with one depends on how often you must empty the tank, whether it stops itself when full and how much it hums at night.

We reviewed six compact units and ranked them on listed tank size, coverage, safety features and noise claims. Every one sits under the $100 mark, and one near-duplicate listing was left out. No listing gives a decibel figure, so noise claims remain claims. Start with the room you want to dry, then pick the tank to match it.

products.name: Dehumidifier 1657ML 58OZ Small Dehumidifier for Home 230 Ft² Safety
products.verdict: The largest listed tank, with defrost and safety protection.
products.description:
This dehumidifier has a 1657 ml (58 oz) tank, a 230 square foot coverage rating and defrost and safety protection, with three quiet setting modes, at $25 to $50. Defrost protection matters in cool rooms, where frost can form on a cooling surface and block airflow. The tank is the largest among the six, so you walk to the sink less often.

It is also the only one here that states a square-foot coverage figure, which is the single number that tells you whether it suits your room. Everything else in the group leaves you guessing.

Best for a bedroom or small room. The caveat is that 230 square feet is a small-room rating, so skip it if you need a whole-basement unit. The brand is not named in the listing, which weakens support options.

products.name: NeedDuck Dehumidifier for Home Small Quiet Dehumidifiers for 44OZ Water Tank
products.verdict: A quiet, compact unit with a 44 oz tank and built-in safety.
products.description:
NeedDuck is a compact, portable dehumidifier with a 44 oz water tank, built-in safety and convenience features and a quiet design, at $25 to $50. The listing contrasts it with high-power machines: its goal is steady, unobtrusive operation, not fast moisture removal.

It gives up 14 oz of tank capacity to the leader, and in exchange emphasizes quiet. That is a deliberate tradeoff, and for a person who sleeps lightly it is the right one. A smaller tank also keeps the unit light to carry from room to room.

It suits light moisture in bedrooms. The caveat is that it is not built for fast removal, and the listing gives no coverage rating. If your room feels clammy after rain, the 58 oz model has more headroom and states its coverage.

products.name: OWAAE Dehumidifier for Home with Auto Shutoff Sleep Mode
products.verdict: Auto shutoff and a sleep mode for nighttime use.
products.description:
The OWAAE offers auto shutoff, a sleep mode and an ultra-quiet design aimed at bedrooms and nighttime comfort, and the listing says it suits bathrooms and enclosed spaces, at $50 to $100. Auto shutoff is the safety piece: it cuts power when the tank is full, which protects the floor if you are asleep or away.

It costs more than the first two picks yet lists no tank size, so you pay for the sleep mode and shutoff without knowing how long a night's run will last. A small hidden tank would fill and stop before morning.

It suits light sleepers who want protection. The caveat is the missing capacity figure. Ask the seller for tank size before buying, or choose NeedDuck, which states 44 oz for less.

products.name: NineSky Dehumidifiers for Home
products.verdict: A quiet unit with smart auto shut-off protection.
products.description:
The NineSky is a quiet, high-efficiency dehumidifier with smart auto shut-off protection, in the $50 to $100 range. It gives you the safety shutoff and a quiet claim, with an efficiency pitch that the listing never quantifies.

Compared with the OWAAE it offers a similar quiet and shutoff story with less emphasis on sleep. The listing gives no tank or coverage figure, so there is nothing to confirm the efficiency claim against.

It suits general home dampness in a small room. The caveat is the thin spec detail, so skip it if you want hard capacity numbers. If shutoff is the main requirement, NineSky and OWAAE are close, and price should decide between them on the day.

products.name: BEDRED Dehumidifier
products.verdict: A semiconductor model with auto shutoff and a 7-color light.
products.description:
The BEDRED is a semiconductor dehumidifier that uses thermoelectric cooling, with intelligent auto shutoff and a 7-color ambient light, at $50 to $100. Thermoelectric units condense water on a cooled plate without a compressor, which makes them compact and quiet but gentle on moisture.

Its thermoelectric design is the distinguishing detail against the rest, and the ambient light is a styling extra. The listing gives no tank size, which makes it hard to rank higher. Small spaces suit it best, such as a wardrobe or a small bathroom.

It suits small spaces where quiet and style matter. The caveat is the missing capacity detail. Skip it if you want strong drying, since this technology moves less water than compressor designs, and check the listing for its stated limits.

products.name: ToLife Dehumidifier
products.verdict: A powerful mode and seven ambient light colors.
products.description:
The ToLife offers a powerful mode and seven ambient light colors, at $50 to $100. A powerful mode implies a boost setting for faster drying, which is the one performance feature the listing mentions.

It is last because the listing leans on lighting rather than stated tank, coverage or shutoff details. Seven colors do nothing for moisture, and a glowing unit in a bedroom can be a nuisance. Without capacity or safety wording, you cannot size it or trust it unattended.

It suits buyers who like ambient lights. The caveat is the sparse spec sheet. Skip it if you want a unit you can leave running overnight, and look at the OWAAE or NineSky, which name a shutoff.

whatMatters.detail: The tank is the water it holds before it needs emptying. A bigger tank means fewer trips to the sink. Look for ounces or milliliters in the title, as on the 58 oz and 44 oz models, and treat a missing figure as a warning that the tank may be small, which would stop the unit sooner than you expect.

Coverage in square feet shows the room size the unit targets. Only one model here lists it, at 230 sq ft. Match the number to your room, and stay at or below it. A unit used in a bigger room runs constantly with little to show for it, and wears out sooner for the same reason.

A full-tank cutoff keeps water from spilling while nobody is home. Check the listing for the words auto shutoff. OWAAE, NineSky and BEDRED state it, while ToLife does not. Without it, a full unit can keep running or overflow, which matters for anything left on overnight or while you are at work.

Quiet matters in bedrooms. Listings here make quiet claims without decibel figures, so treat them as claims, not measurements. Check reviews for real feedback, and compare units with a sleep mode, since lower fan speed usually trades some drying speed for peace, which suits a bedroom better than a laundry room.

Thermoelectric units use a semiconductor, as on the BEDRED. They suit small spaces and run quietly, but they remove less water than compressor designs. Check the type in the description, and match it to your room: closets and bathrooms suit it, a damp basement does not. Plan on emptying the tank regularly even with the smaller models.

faq.q: How large a room will these cover?
faq.a: Only the 58 oz model lists coverage, at 230 sq ft. The others do not, so treat them as small-room units and keep them in a bedroom, closet or bathroom, with the door closed so the unit works on one space.

Expecting a compact unit to dry a whole basement. These suit small spaces, and a larger compressor dehumidifier is the right tool for a big damp area, because these small models cannot keep up with it.

faq.q: Is a bigger tank worth it?
faq.a: Yes if you hate emptying. The 58 oz model lists the largest tank among the six, but a bigger tank also means a heavier unit to carry when full, so empty it before you lift it.
Follow the instructions. The listings we reviewed do not describe the steps, so read the manual, and empty the tank before moving the unit so water does not spill on the floor.

faq.q: Do I need to clean it?
faq.a: Follow the maker's care guide. The listings do not give a cleaning routine, so wipe the tank and intake regularly, because damp parts can grow mildew if left, and a smell is the first sign.

The OWAAE lists a sleep mode and auto shutoff for nighttime use. Check others on the product page, especially the 58 oz model and NineSky, before running them unattended, and never leave any unit running on a surface that could be damaged by a leak.

finalTake: Buy the 58 oz model for a bedroom or small room, or NeedDuck if quiet matters more than tank size. OWAAE suits light sleepers. BEDRED and ToLife rely on features that say little about drying. None of these tackles a whole basement, so match coverage to the space first.
